verdict.rationale: Greptile's own docs explicitly claim thumbs-up/down reactions and replies teach it what matters so it stops repeating unwanted comments after 2-3 weeks (greptile-docs-4), which is exactly this story, and custom rules/strictness settings (greptile-docs-20, greptile-docs-21) reinforce a feedback-tuning mechanism. However this is first-party only — no independent or hands-on evidence confirms the 'learns from a single rejected comment' behavior in practice, and community comments (e.g. greptile-comm-8) describe author reply-and-fix flows but not confirmed suppression of specific previously-rejected feedback. Missing for 10: independent corroboration of the learning loop, and clarity on scope (per-PR vs. team-wide memory).
